Add death, graft failure, rejection and malignancy outcomes

Source: R/add_time_to_event_variables.R
add_time_to_event_outcomes.Rd

Adds an event date, an event indicator, a censoring date and a time for each post-transplant outcome: patient death, all-cause and death-censored graft failure, malignancy and acute rejection. The follow-up forms are read from the matching follow-up file (TX_KI to TXF_KI, and so on) with load_srtr_file(), for the cohort's TRR_IDs only. Defaults follow the SRTR program-specific report methods where SRTR gives a rule; the arguments switch to other common choices.

Usage

add_time_to_event_outcomes(
  df,
  death_window = c("ascertainment", "follow_up"),
  ascertainment_date = "TFL_ENDTXFU",
  graft_death_same_day = c("censor", "event"),
  rejection_after_graft_failure = c("exclude", "keep"),
  retransplant = c("graft_failure", "ignore")
)

Arguments

df

A transplant data frame from load_srtr_file(). Its file_key attribute decides which follow-up file and outcome columns are used.

death_window

Which deaths count as events, and where recipients without one are censored:

  • "ascertainment" (default): the SRTR program-specific report method for patient survival. Deaths from any source on or before ascertainment_date count; everyone else is assumed alive and censored at that date, even if their last follow-up form is earlier.

  • "follow_up": deaths on or before the recipient's last follow-up date count; everyone else is censored at last follow-up.

sRtr's defaults follow SRTR's published definitions where SRTR gives one; other practice is available as an option.

ascertainment_date

Where death ascertainment ends, used when death_window = "ascertainment". Either the name of a date column with one date per recipient, or one date for everyone (a Date or text such as "2023-06-30"). The default, "TFL_ENDTXFU", is the column SRTR describes as the last possible follow-up date for each transplant, with a built-in lag of 3 months. A recipient whose date is missing gets no death event and a missing time, with a warning.

graft_death_same_day

How to treat a graft failure dated on the day the recipient died:

  • "censor" (default): as death with a functioning graft. The graft is censored at death, not counted as failed.

  • "event": as a graft failure.

The default is a package assumption, not an SRTR rule: the data dictionary does not say whether the graft failure date is filled in with the death date when a recipient dies with a functioning graft. A real failure and death can also fall on the same day. Run both settings to see how much your results depend on it.

rejection_after_graft_failure

Whether a rejection reported after the graft failed counts:

  • "exclude" (default): a graft is at risk of rejection only until it fails. Forms filed in the years after graft failure are not used, and the rejection window ends at the graft failure date (TFL_GRAFT_DT, or that graft's own date, TFL_GRAFT_DT_KI or TFL_GRAFT_DT_PA, for TX_KP); grafts without a rejection are censored there. These columns are then required.

  • "keep": every form counts, as before.

The follow-up code TFL_FOL_CD uses format FOLCD of the SRTR data dictionary (SAF releases 2203 and 2609): code 800 is the form filed at graft failure and codes 801 to 850 are "N year after graft failure". Under "exclude", sRtr leaves out codes 801 to 850. These are package conventions, not SRTR rules: the form filed at failure (code 800) is kept, since it may report the rejection that led to the failure; a rejection reported on the day of failure counts; and a rejection during the transplant admission counts if it falls inside the ordinary window, even when the graft failed in the same admission (its date is only a discharge-date proxy). Censoring still ends at the failure date.

Malignancy is patient-level and always uses every form. The columns from add_txf_outcomes() (FIRST_FU_REJ_DATE, FIRST_FU_REJ_STATUS) describe every form either way.

retransplant

Whether a retransplant ends the graft in the all-cause graft failure outcome (GRAFT_FAIL_ALL_CAUSE_DT):

  • "graft_failure" (default): the retransplant date (PERS_RETX, or PERS_RETXKI and PERS_RETXPA for TX_KP) counts as graft failure, as in the SRTR program-specific reports. It never counts for lung and heart-lung (TX_LU, TX_HL), which SRTR also leaves it out for.

  • "ignore": retransplant is not used.

The death-censored graft failure columns (TFL_GRAFT_DT_*) do not use retransplant either way.

Value

df with these columns added. For each outcome, _CENSOR is the event date if the event counts, else the censoring date; _BINARY is 1 for a counted event, else 0; _days is the time from REC_TX_DT to _CENSOR (see srtr_time_to_event()).

  • Death: REC_DEATH_DT_COMPOSITE with _source and _conflict (see srtr_composite_death()), then _CENSOR, _BINARY, _days.

  • All-cause graft failure: GRAFT_FAIL_ALL_CAUSE_DT, _SOURCE, _CENSOR, _BINARY, _days.

  • Death-censored graft failure: TFL_GRAFT_DT_CENSOR, _BINARY, _days.

  • Malignancy: FIRST_FU_MALIG_DATE, FIRST_FU_MALIG_STATUS, FIRST_FU_MALIG_LAST_NEG_DATE (see add_txf_outcomes()), then FIRST_FU_MALIG_DATE_CENSOR, _BINARY, _days and _DEATH_DAY.

  • Rejection: FIRST_FU_REJ_DATE, FIRST_FU_REJ_STATUS, FIRST_FU_REJ_LAST_NEG_DATE, FIRST_REJ_DATE (the date used) and FIRST_REJ_DATE_SOURCE, then FIRST_REJ_DATE_CENSOR, _BINARY, _days and _DEATH_DAY.

For TX_KP, graft columns come once per graft with _KI and _PA (GRAFT_FAIL_ALL_CAUSE_DT_KI, TFL_GRAFT_DT_PA_CENSOR, FIRST_FU_REJ_DATE_KI, ...); kidney rejection keeps the name FIRST_REJ_DATE, and pancreas rejection is FIRST_REJ_DATE_PA. The txf_report attribute from add_txf_outcomes() is kept.

Details

It accepts all eight transplant files (TX_KI, TX_LI, TX_PA, TX_KP, TX_HR, TX_LU, TX_HL and TX_IN), whose columns the SRTR data dictionary lists. So far only TX_LI has been checked on a real release; check the others on your own files (see the Checking sRtr on your own SAFs guide).

REC_DEATH_DT_COMPOSITE keeps every death date from every source. Only the event and censoring columns (REC_DEATH_DT_COMPOSITE_BINARY, _CENSOR, _days) depend on death_window. Counting deaths found after last follow-up while censoring survivors at last follow-up would overstate mortality (#18).

Two graft failure outcomes are added. All-cause graft failure (GRAFT_FAIL_ALL_CAUSE_DT, or GRAFT_FAIL_ALL_CAUSE_DT_KI and GRAFT_FAIL_ALL_CAUSE_DT_PA for TX_KP) follows the SRTR program-specific reports: the graft fails at the first of its graft failure date, retransplant (see retransplant) and death from any source (REC_DEATH_DT_COMPOSITE). The graft is censored at its last follow-up date, and an event after that date is not counted. Heart grafts (TX_HR) follow SRTR's heart rule instead: only death and retransplant count, the graft failure date is not used, and follow-up is not censored at the last follow-up date but ends where death ascertainment ends (see death_window). The date column holds the first event even when it is not counted, and _SOURCE says which it was ("graft_failure", "retransplant" or "death"; on the same day, in that order).

As in the SRTR reports, a graft is censored on the day of transplant, with no event, when any of its graft failure, retransplant or death dates falls before the transplant date (_SOURCE is then "before_transplant", and a later event is not used in its place), or when its last follow-up date is missing or before the transplant date. Its time is then the one-day offset that srtr_time_to_event() adds.

Death-censored graft failure (TFL_GRAFT_DT, or TFL_GRAFT_DT_KI and TFL_GRAFT_DT_PA for TX_KP) is not an SRTR report definition, and does not depend on death_window: a graft failure dated after the recipient's death from any source (REC_DEATH_DT_COMPOSITE) is not counted, and a graft without a failure is censored at the earlier of its last follow-up date and death. Death with a functioning graft is a censoring time, not a graft failure. A graft failure dated after the last follow-up date but before death is still counted, at its own date.

First rejection (FIRST_REJ_DATE, and FIRST_REJ_DATE_PA for TX_KP) counts a treated rejection (code 1 of format ACREJEP, raw or labelled) during the transplant admission (REC_ACUTE_REJ_EPISODE, or REC_ACUTE_REJ_EPISODE_PA) first, else the first follow-up form reporting one. An admission rejection is dated at discharge, a proxy: the transplant date plus REC_POSTX_LOS, else REC_DISCHRG_DT; a date before the transplant is not used. FIRST_REJ_DATE_SOURCE ("admission_los", "admission_discharge", "admission_undated" or "follow_up") says which rule applied ("follow_up_undated" is described below). Here a missing date does not always mean no event: an admission rejection with no usable date keeps _BINARY = 1 with a missing censoring date and time, with a warning, so it drops out of time-to-event models instead of counting as rejection-free. A later follow-up rejection stays in FIRST_FU_REJ_DATE (FIRST_FU_REJ_DATE_KI and FIRST_FU_REJ_DATE_PA for TX_KP, with FIRST_REJ_DATE_PA_SOURCE for the pancreas) and is never used in its place. A date is unusable when it falls before the transplant; with no transplant date, the discharge date is kept, and the elapsed time is missing.

Malignancy (FIRST_FU_MALIG_DATE) and rejection count only inside the window the recipient or graft is followed for: from the transplant date up to the earlier of the last follow-up date and death from any source (REC_DEATH_DT_COMPOSITE), both inclusive, whatever death_window is. Malignancy uses the patient's last follow-up (for TX_KP, the later of the two graft dates); rejection uses the graft's own (TFL_LAFUDATEKI or TFL_LAFUDATEPA for TX_KP). Without an event, the recipient is censored at the end of the window. A report dated after it is not an event, but its date stays in the date column, so !is.na(FIRST_FU_MALIG_DATE) & FIRST_FU_MALIG_DATE_BINARY == 0 finds the reports left out. A report dated before the transplant is not used: events are timed from the first report on or after the transplant date, while FIRST_FU_MALIG_DATE and FIRST_FU_REJ_DATE keep the first report of all, for auditing (FIRST_REJ_DATE is the date used). With no last follow-up date the window's end is unknown: death is not used in its place, and the time is missing.

A malignancy or rejection reported only on follow-up forms with no date (status "event" with a missing date in add_txf_outcomes()) is treated like an undated admission rejection: _BINARY = 1 with a missing censoring date and time, with a warning, so it does not add event-free time. For rejection, FIRST_REJ_DATE_SOURCE is then "follow_up_undated".

Follow-up dates are report dates (see add_txf_outcomes()). A report dated on the day of death may come from the form filed at death, so the event may have happened earlier. FIRST_FU_MALIG_DATE_DEATH_DAY and FIRST_REJ_DATE_DEATH_DAY (and FIRST_REJ_DATE_PA_DEATH_DAY) are TRUE when the date is the day of death, FALSE when it is another day, and NA with no date, so you can run a sensitivity analysis without those events. Such reports count as events by default when follow-up covers the day of death. The status columns from add_txf_outcomes() say what the forms report, before the window is applied.

References

Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients. Technical Methods for the Program-Specific Reports, section C, patient survival and graft survival. https://srtr.hrsa.gov/transplant-professionals/program-specific-report/technical-methods-for-the-program-specific-reports/

Kim SJ, Snyder JJ. OPTN/SRTR registry analysis: the devil is in the details. Slides, American Transplant Congress; 2012. Slide 25 (TFL_ENDTXFU). https://www.srtr.org/media/1106/atc2012_snyder_kim.pdf

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
tx <- load_srtr_file("TX_LI")
tx <- add_time_to_event_outcomes(tx)
table(tx$GRAFT_FAIL_ALL_CAUSE_DT_SOURCE, tx$GRAFT_FAIL_ALL_CAUSE_DT_BINARY)

# Censor deaths at the last follow-up form instead
tx <- add_time_to_event_outcomes(load_srtr_file("TX_LI"), death_window = "follow_up")
} # }
